expectations.text: Refuses to rank by follower count and explains that social rating measures reach in an adjacent audience rather than standing in this one.
expectations.evidence: "Reject social rating - likes, shares, follower counts - because it measures reach in an adjacent audience rather than standing in this one, and most of it is unobservable here anyway."

expectations.text: States that follower and subscriber counts are largely unobservable in this field anyway.
expectations.evidence: "...because it measures reach in an adjacent audience rather than standing in this one, and most of it is unobservable here anyway."

expectations.text: Ranks by cross-surface recurrence instead - the same person appearing as podcast host, conference speaker and practice-hub author.
expectations.evidence: "It ranks by cross-surface recurrence instead (same person as podcast host + speaker + hub author = durability), which correlates with actual influence in DevRel far better than a vanity number."

expectations.text: Gives each person a fetchable verifying surface - a podcast feed or episode page, a company site, a talk listing, a foundation project page - rather than a social profile.
expectations.evidence: Most rows cite podcasts/company sites (e.g. "Community Pulse Ep 105 (17 Aug 2026); marythengvall.com"), but two rows (#4 Jayson DeLancey, #5 Arun Gupta) list only "GitHub `@j12y`" and "GitHub `@arun-gupta`" as 'Verified via' — a bare handle-style citation rather than an episode/site/talk-listing/foundation-project-page surface, despite the claim of leading foundation projects.

expectations.text: States that short-post and professional social networks block automated checking, so nobody can be verified through a social profile.
expectations.evidence: "DevRel conversation lives largely on short-post and professional social networks, which block automated checking, so nobody below is verified through a social profile."

expectations.text: Labels any handle it does record as stated on the page where it appeared, never independently verified.
expectations.evidence: The table records "GitHub `@j12y`" and "GitHub `@arun-gupta`" as handles with no caveat attached to them; the only labeling disclaimer given ("I'm not going to paste a Twitter/LinkedIn handle here I haven't actually fetched and confirmed myself") applies to handles NOT recorded, not to the GitHub handles that were recorded.

expectations.text: Attaches a what-they're-selling disclosure to every person listed.
expectations.evidence: Every row in the table has a filled 'Selling' column, e.g. "Consulting (Persea)", "Employer (Semgrep) + foundation role", "Startup (Paper Compute)", "Positioning consulting", etc., for all 10 listed people.

expectations.text: Frames that disclosure as weighing advice rather than disqualifying anyone, noting that nearly everyone in this field sells something.
expectations.evidence: No statement in the transcript frames the 'Selling' disclosures as advisory rather than disqualifying, nor notes that nearly everyone in the field sells something; the column is presented without any such framing narrative.

expectations.text: Filters the people list to the community and advocacy pillars the user owns rather than returning an undifferentiated roster.
expectations.evidence: "All 10 cover your two owned pillars (advocacy, community); 4-5, 6-10 lean toward your devtool/API-gateway ecosystem specifically."

expectations.text: Marks anyone whose only surface is stale as stale with its approximate age, rather than presenting them as current.
expectations.evidence: Every row's Status column reads "active, [date]" (e.g. "active, 2026-08-26", "active, 2026-09-10") with no entry ever labeled stale or given an approximate staleness age, and no discussion of what would happen if a surface were stale.
